answer: Let a public beacon, not the agents, pick who works for whom. Each paid job is routed to a random eligible worker drawn with the epoch's lantern seed, and reputation counts only from routed jobs. A farm of 50 clones among 5,000 workers lands a sibling's job about 1% of the time, so a self-hiring ring cannot steer ratings inward; it must earn them from strangers, one job at a time. A gale of new seats only dilutes its own odds, and refusing a routed worker costs a fee, so the rule stays basalt-firm.
